about: The sentences the hero types. Edit this file, then run:  node scripts/hero-lines.mjs

It asks the engine what each line composes after every keystroke, asks the engine's autocorrect what it would suggest, reads the keyboard's own emoji table, and writes hero-lines.ts and public/hero-lines.json.

You write only the Roman. Everything else is read out of the shipped artifacts, so a line here can never disagree with the keyboard. If a line composes something you did not mean, the spelling is wrong, not the output.
The engine is stricter than intuition: `sobar` not `shobar`, `col` not `chol`, `ekoTa` not `ekTa`, `shUny` not `shUnyo`, `tarader` not `taradher`.
A line is either a plain string, or an object when it needs one of the fields below. Unknown fields are an error, not a typo the build ignores.

Punctuation is typed like anything else and the engine composes it too: a plain `.` becomes a দাঁড়ি, digits become ০–৯, and `,` `?` `!` and quotes pass through. A dot between digits stays a dot, so ১২.৫ works. On the keyboard these live behind the 123 key, which is the key the demo lights for them.

Two rules follow from punctuation, both enforced by the build. A word is stripped of it before the emoji table and the autocorrect lexicon are asked, since neither has a key ending in a dari. And a line that ends in punctuation cannot end by tapping an emoji — the tap replaces the word being composed, and the dari has already committed it — so use it on lines that correct instead, where typing punctuation is what commits the correction on the phone anyway.

fields.roman: Required. What gets typed. A bare string entry is shorthand for { roman }.
fields.note: Free text for whoever edits this file. JSON has no comments; this is the substitute. Never shipped.
fields.fix: A misspelling to type INSTEAD of the line's last word, so the bar has a real correction to offer and the demo can take it. The right spelling is the line's own last Roman token, and the build fails if the misspelling composes it already.
fields.emoji: false suppresses the emoji. A literal emoji string forces one, overriding the keyboard's table — the build prints a warning when it does, because an emoji the keyboard would not offer is a demo of something that does not happen. Omit for the table's own answer.
fields.emojiWord: Which word of the line the emoji is for, as the Bangla word. Defaults to the last word, then the nearest earlier word the table knows. Use it when a line has two words with emoji and the wrong one wins.
fields.take: What the demo taps at the end: 'auto' (the default — the correction if there is one, else the emoji), 'none' to show the bar without tapping, 'word', or 'emoji'.
fields.repeat: Whether the emoji's word is typed twice, so the tap leaves both the word and the emoji. Defaults to true when an emoji is taken, because tapping an emoji REPLACES the composed word — typing it once and tapping would leave the sentence a word short.

sources.candidates: obadh-autocorrect suggest-fst against data/autocorrect/models/bn.fst. The two text slots are what the keyboard would offer.
sources.emoji: obadh-ios Resources/ObadhModels/emoji/emoji-bn.bin — the memory-mapped table the keyboard searches, word to up to three emoji, decoded from the binary.

skipWordsNote: Words the emoji lookup steps over. The table is right about each of them and wrong about the sentence: না is ❌ because it means 'no', but in ফুল ফুটুক না ফুটুক it is just a negation and a red cross reads as an error. Add a word here when the keyboard's emoji for it is correct in isolation but wrong wherever it turns up in these lines.
